thesis: CG Oncology rose about 13.8% to $84.69 (from $74.40) on 8.3x volume after its PIVOT-006 Phase 3 trial of cretostimogene in bladder cancer met its primary endpoint, cutting recurrence risk by 68% versus control (hazard ratio 0.32). The shares were up as much as about 31% premarket and touched a 52-week high of $93.95 at the open before fading. Counter-cases remain open: the BLA for cretostimogene is still being completed, with no FDA acceptance or PDUFA date found, so approval and launch timing are not yet confirmed; and the fade from the open shows the market has not settled on the data's value. The litigation check found Kuehn Law's August 2026 fiduciary-duty investigation of officers and directors (a solicitation, with no filed suit found) and a 2025 Delaware jury verdict in the company's favor in the ANI Pharmaceuticals royalty case; no restatement found. This run found no company press release or wire report for the data, so a confirmed, company-specific trial win with the regulatory path still pending makes this medium.
invalidation: Full PIVOT-006 data show a safety or durability problem, the BLA is delayed or not accepted, or a close back below the pre-data level (~$74.40).

thesis: Ingram Micro fell about 3.1% to $27.54 (from $28.42) on 4.6x volume, and this run found no company news dated today. The most recent company-specific item found is supply-related: Platinum Equity's affiliate sold 11M shares at $25.90 in a secondary offering that settled around Nov 4 (the company bought back 1M shares and received no proceeds), and Platinum still owns about 164.3M shares, roughly 71% of shares outstanding, after earlier sales in March and September. The litigation check found a $350K class settlement over the July 2025 cyberattack (Rodden v. Ingram Micro Americas) and a plaintiff-firm investigation of a January 2026 breach disclosure, with no scheduled ruling found and no restatement. A move with no identified company catalyst under a continuing sponsor-supply overhang makes this low; avoid.
invalidation: Sponsor selling pauses and a company-disclosed result drives the shares.

thesis: Chime rose about 2.1% to $34.26 (from $33.55) on 4.1x volume, about 3.6% below its 52-week high; this run found no company news dated today. The company-specific catalyst on record is the Nov 4 Q3 report (8-K): revenue grew 32% to $718M, accelerating from 27% in Q2; net income was $44M, a third straight quarter of GAAP profitability; adjusted EBITDA was $137M (19% margin); active members grew 20% to 10.9M; and Q4 and full-year guidance was raised (Q4 revenue $757-767M, 27-29% growth). Counter-cases remain open: today's volume spike has no identified driver, and this run did not check for a lock-up expiry or sponsor sale that could add supply. The litigation check found no lawsuit, investigation or restatement. A confirmed beat-and-raise with today's driver unidentified makes this medium.
invalidation: Revenue growth slows below the raised guide, member growth stalls, or a close back below ~$33.55.
sources: StockAnalysis (CHYM quote page, analyst targets): https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/chym/

thesis: Mobility Global rose about 3.3% to $24.045 (from $23.28) on 2.5x volume, extending a gain of about 15% to a new 52-week high on Nov 12 after its Q3 report: revenue of $478M and adjusted EPS of $0.40 beat estimates of $475M and $0.38, and CARFAX segment revenue grew 8% to $313M. The company authorized an $800M buyback in October. Counter-cases remain open: management flagged B2B sales-cycle delays tied to macro conditions, analyst views are mixed (BofA Neutral with a $25 target; Baird cut to $22, Neutral; Morgan Stanley equal-weight at $19), and the company carries $2B of senior notes issued ahead of its July 1, 2026 spin-off from S&P Global (debt, not equity). The litigation check found no lawsuit, investigation or restatement. A confirmed beat with growth and leverage counter-cases unresolved makes this medium.
invalidation: CARFAX growth slows below mid-single digits, B2B delays widen into a guidance cut, or a close back below the pre-report level (~$19.92).
sources: S&P Global (senior notes ahead of separation): https://press.spglobal.com/2026-05-19-S-P-Global-Announces-Pricing-of-2,000,000,000-Private-Offering-of-Senior-Notes-by-Mobility-Global-Inc-Ahead-of-Planned-Separation?asPDF=1

thesis: Tyson rose about 8.7% to $63.96 (from $58.82) on 2.3x volume after its Nov 16 fiscal Q4 report (8-K): sales were $14.585B (from $13.86B), adjusted EPS was $0.61, $300M of stock was repurchased in the quarter, the quarterly dividend was raised to $0.52, and coverage of the call highlights an improved beef outlook for fiscal 2027. Counter-cases remain open: fiscal 2026 adjusted EPS fell 17% to $3.44, beef posted a $654M adjusted operating loss for the year with an $80M Q4 write-down on tight cattle supplies, the company forecasts lower sales in fiscal 2027, and sources disagree on whether Q4 EPS beat consensus. Litigation: Tyson settled beef price-fixing claims with direct purchasers ($82.5M, January 2026) and indirect purchasers ($55M) and pork claims ($48M), with final-approval status not confirmed and no scheduled trial found; no restatement found. A confirmed report with an improving beef outlook and these counter-cases unresolved makes this medium.
invalidation: Beef losses do not narrow as guided, fiscal 2027 guidance is cut, or a close back below the pre-report level (~$58.82).
sources: Investing.com (earnings call, shares jump on outlook): https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-tyson-foods-posts-q4-miss-but-shares-jump-on-outlook-93CH-5030386

thesis: Keurig Dr Pepper fell about 2.0% to $35.61 (from $36.34) on 2.1x volume as it completed its common stock offering on Nov 16: 57,971,015 shares priced at $34.50 plus the full 8,695,652-share underwriter option, for about $2.25B of net proceeds to repay debt ahead of its planned business split. thesis: Wolverine World Wide rose about 1.8% to $25.34 (from $24.89) on 2.3x volume, touching a new 52-week high of $25.60, and is up about 29% over 60 days. The company-specific catalyst on record is its fiscal Q3 report: adjusted EPS of $0.79 versus the $0.46 estimate and revenue of $505.4M versus about $500M; UBS raised its target to $31. Counter-cases remain open: this run did not confirm the report date or full-year guidance, the former President of the Active Group (Merrell, Saucony) left effective Oct 31, 2026 under a separation agreement (a segment president, with no execution problem cited), and PFAS exposure continues: a February 2026 dispute with Michigan over the scope of a settlement obligation and a December 2025 suit by two landfills against Wolverine and 3M, with no scheduled ruling found. No restatement was found. A large earnings beat with legacy PFAS exposure unresolved makes this medium.
invalidation: Revenue growth stalls in the next report, PFAS costs rise materially, or a close back below ~$23.85 (the Nov 13 high).

thesis: Payoneer was unchanged at $7.20 on 2.2x volume, $0.20 (about 2.8%) below the $7.40-per-share cash price Nuvei agreed to pay (about $2.75B, June 2026). The near-52-week-high and volume signals reflect deal-bound trading as the definitive proxy has been filed; closing is expected in mid-2027, subject to shareholder and regulatory approvals, including licenses in China and India that are central to the deal. The proxy says the company is not aware of any pending lawsuit challenging the merger, though one stockholder sent a disclosure-demand letter, and several law firms (Ademi, Monteverde, Wohl & Fruchter, Halper Sadeh) announced investigations; no restatement found. Upside is capped at the deal price, so the move is mechanical; low, avoid.
invalidation: The merger agreement is terminated or its terms change, so the stock trades on fundamentals again.

thesis: H World rose about 9.0% to $54.91 (from $50.39) on 2.1x volume, about 3% below its 52-week high, after its Nov 16 Q3 report (GlobeNewswire): revenue rose 11.3% to RMB7.75B, above the ~RMB7.33B estimate; net income rose to RMB1.8B from RMB1.5B; HWC guidance was raised to 13-14% from 7-11%; and full-year 2026 revenue growth guidance was raised to 9-10% from 4-8%. invalidation: HWI revenue keeps declining, the raised revenue guide is cut, or a close back below the pre-report level (~$50.39).
